name: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
summary: Obsessions and/or compulsions that are time-consuming or impairing. FDA-labeled drugs are clomipramine and the SSRIs fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, and sertraline (pediatric labeling for clomipramine 10+, fluoxetine 7+, fluvoxamine IR 8+, sertraline 6+). Exposure and response prevention (ERP) is first-line psychotherapy. Troriluzole failed Phase 3 and was dropped for OCD in 2025.
plainSummary: OCD causes unwanted, repeated thoughts and urges to do things over and over, like checking or washing. A type of therapy called ERP and certain antidepressants can help, often at higher doses.

approved.indication: Treatment of obsessions and compulsions in patients with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD).

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 10 years and older

dosing.target: About 100 mg/day by the end of week 2, then titrate over several weeks
dosing.max: Adults: 250 mg/day; children/adolescents: 3 mg/kg/day or 200 mg/day, whichever is smaller
dosing.notes: Give in divided doses with meals during titration; once daily at bedtime after titration. Pediatric: up to 3 mg/kg or 100 mg (whichever smaller) in the first 2 weeks. Steady state takes 2–3 weeks. Seizure risk is dose-related; cardiac conduction effects; lethal in overdose.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to clomipramine or other tricyclic antidepressants
MAOIs concurrently or within 14 days; starting in patients on linezolid or IV methylene blue
Acute recovery period after myocardial infarction
approved.plainSummary: Clomipramine is an older antidepressant approved for OCD in adults and children 10 and older. It works well but has more side effects than SSRIs.

approved.indication: Acute and maintenance treatment of obsessions and compulsions in patients with Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD).

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 7 years and older

dosing.start: Adults: 20 mg/day in the morning; pediatric: 10 mg/day
dosing.target: Adults: 20–60 mg/day; pediatric: 20–60 mg/day (adolescents and higher-weight children) or 20–30 mg/day (lower-weight children)
dosing.max: 80 mg/day (adults); pediatric experience above 60 mg/day is lacking
dosing.notes: Full effect may take 5 weeks or longer. Pediatric (higher weight): increase to 20 mg after 2 weeks. Doses above 20 mg/day may be given once daily or split morning and noon.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs concurrently, within 5 weeks of stopping fluoxetine, or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI; starting in patients on linezolid or IV methylene blue
Thioridazine (and within 5 weeks of stopping fluoxetine)
approved.plainSummary: Fluoxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for OCD in adults and children 7 and older. OCD often needs higher doses and more time than depression.

verified.note: Indication, pediatric ages (7–17), and dosing confirmed on the label. Adult OCD approval year (1994) not re-confirmed in Drugs@FDA. Drugs@FDA lists Prozac capsules as discontinued; generics available.

approved.indication: Treatment of obsessions and compulsions in patients with obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) (IR tablets); treatment of OCD (ER capsules).

population.ages: Adults (IR and ER); pediatric patients 8–17 years (IR tablets only)

dosing.start: IR adults: 50 mg at bedtime; IR ages 8–17: 25 mg at bedtime; ER adults: 100 mg at bedtime
dosing.notes: IR: increase by 50 mg (adults) or 25 mg (pediatric) every 4–7 days; split doses above 100 mg/day (adults) or 50 mg/day (pediatric). ER: increase by 50 mg weekly; not evaluated in pediatric patients. Slower titration in elderly or hepatic impairment. Potent CYP1A2/2C19 inhibitor.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: Tizanidine, thioridazine, pimozide, or alosetron (plus ramelteon for ER)
MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Fluvoxamine is an SSRI approved for OCD in adults and in children 8 and older (regular tablets). It interacts with many other medicines.

verified.note: ER label also checked: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=49601858-df61-4522-ac99-0d2892f92e11. Luvox and Luvox CR brands discontinued (Drugs@FDA); Luvox CR approved 2008. Pediatric OCD for IR added 1997.

approved.indication: Treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) in adults (Paxil immediate-release; Paxil CR is not labeled for OCD).

dosing.target: Increase by 10 mg/day weekly as needed
dosing.notes: Geriatric, severe renal or hepatic impairment: start 10 mg/day, max 40 mg/day. Taper to stop.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
Drugs that prolong the QTc interval and are CYP2D6 substrates (e.g., thioridazine, pimozide)
approved.plainSummary: Paroxetine is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for OCD in adults.

verified.note: The Sept 2026 label no longer states a specific target dose for OCD (older labels said 40 mg/day).

population.ages: Adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older

dosing.start: Adults and ages 13–17: 50 mg once daily; ages 6–12: 25 mg once daily
dosing.notes: Increase by 25–50 mg/day once weekly. Mild hepatic impairment: half the usual dose. Sertraline 150/200 mg capsules (labeled for MDD and OCD) are not for initiation.

boxedWarnings: Suicidal thoughts and behaviors in children, adolescents, and young adults
contraindications: MAOIs (including linezolid or IV methylene blue) concurrently or within 14 days
approved.plainSummary: Sertraline is a daily antidepressant (SSRI) approved for OCD in adults and children 6 and older.

verified.note: Sertraline capsules label also checked: https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=23f1c8c5-032c-4ea9-beb0-ca3a614ba4b6. Pediatric OCD added 1997.

offLabel.use: SSRI-resistant OCD (added to an SSRI or clomipramine)
offLabel.notes: APA and NICE list antipsychotic augmentation for partial or non-response; meta-analysis supports low-dose risperidone. Benefit is modest (roughly one-third respond). Cautions: weight gain, metabolic effects, hyperprolactinemia, EPS/tardive dyskinesia.

references.label: Veale et al. 2014, BMC Psychiatry: Atypical antipsychotic augmentation in SSRI-refractory OCD, meta-analysis
APA OCD Practice Guideline (2007) and 2013 Guideline Watch (Psychiatric News summary)
NICE CG31: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder (recommendations)

offLabel.notes: Supported by small RCTs and meta-analysis; NICE recommends antipsychotic augmentation as a class. Cautions: akathisia, metabolic effects, impulse-control problems. Quetiapine and olanzapine augmentation have weaker evidence.

references.label: Veale et al. 2014, BMC Psychiatry: Atypical antipsychotic augmentation in SSRI-refractory OCD, meta-analysis
NICE CG31: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder (recommendations)

offLabel.notes: Higher SSRI doses give modestly greater benefit in OCD, with more dropouts from side effects. APA describes doses above the labeled maximum in some patients with close monitoring. Avoid supratherapeutic citalopram/escitalopram (QT) and watch interactions.

references.label: Bloch et al. 2010, Molecular Psychiatry: Dose-response of SSRIs in OCD, meta-analysis
APA OCD Practice Guideline (2007) and 2013 Guideline Watch (Psychiatric News summary)

offLabel.notes: NICE lists citalopram among first-line SSRIs for adult OCD; neither is FDA-labeled for OCD. Dose-related QT prolongation with citalopram (FDA max 40 mg/day; 20 mg/day over age 60).

references.label: NICE CG31: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and body dysmorphic disorder (recommendations)
APA OCD Practice Guideline (2007) and 2013 Guideline Watch (Psychiatric News summary)
